target: Mi lasci il suo numero, la richiameremo noi.
english: Leave me your number, we'll call you back.
tip: Formal Lei commands use the subjunctive form, so lasciare becomes lasci, not the informal lascia.

target: Senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse, il tempo era passato.
english: Without anyone noticing, time had passed.
tip: Senza che takes the subjunctive and pairs with nessuno where English says 'anyone': senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse.

target: L'azienda per la quale mia madre ha lavorato per vent'anni ha chiuso i battenti.
english: The company my mother worked for twenty years closed down.
tip: Per la quale is the formal written version of per cui, and la quale agrees with feminine l'azienda.

target: A meno che non ci sia traffico, arriviamo puntuali.
english: Unless there's traffic, we'll arrive on time.
tip: In a meno che non ci sia, the non is pleonastic, not a real negation: it means unless there is traffic.

target: Ha perso le chiavi di casa, il che significa che dobbiamo chiamare il fabbro.
english: He lost the house keys, which means we have to call the locksmith.
tip: Il che points back to the whole previous statement, not a single noun, which is why significa follows it.

target: Avendo finito il lavoro, uscì.
english: Having finished work, he left.
tip: Avendo plus a participle marks an action finished before the main verb: Avendo finito il lavoro = having finished work.

target: Ha fatto costruire una casa nuova.
english: He had a new house built.
tip: Fare plus an infinitive means to get something done by others. Ha fatto costruire una casa = he had a house built, he did not build it himself.

target: Purché venga fatta giustizia, accetterò qualsiasi verdetto.
english: As long as justice is done, I'll accept any verdict.
tip: Purché means 'provided that' and always takes the subjunctive: Purché venga fatta giustizia = as long as justice is done.

target: Lungi dall'essere risolto, il problema si è aggravato.
english: Far from being resolved, the problem has worsened.
tip: Lungi is an archaic 'far' that survives only in this formula: Lungi dall'essere risolto = far from being resolved.

target: La donna il cui figlio è il mio compagno di classe.
english: The woman whose son is my classmate.
tip: Il cui means whose. The article agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: il matches figlio, not the donna who owns it.

target: Ce la metto tutta.
english: I'm giving it my all.
tip: In Ce la metto tutta the ce and la are frozen bits of mettercela tutta; la points at nothing, and that's the trap.

target: Ho fatto riparare la macchina.
english: I had the car repaired.
tip: Fare plus an infinitive means someone else does it for you: Ho fatto riparare la macchina = I had the car repaired.

target: Non ce la faccio più!
english: I can't take it anymore!
tip: Farcela means to manage or cope; here ce and la are fixed inside the verb and più adds 'anymore': Non ce la faccio più.

target: Se la prende per tutto.
english: He gets upset about everything.
tip: Prendersela means to get upset or take it personally; add con for the target: Se la prende con me.

target: Andando avanti così, non finiremo mai.
english: Going on like this, we'll never finish.
tip: A bare gerund covers English 'if' or 'by' with no separate word: Andando avanti così = if we go on like this.

target: Foss'anche l'ultima cosa che faccio, lo porterò a termine.
english: Even if it were the last thing I do, I'll see it through.
tip: Foss'anche means 'were it even'. It is fosse (were) elided, and Italian drops se, so the inverted verb alone carries the 'even if'.

target: Non fosse stato per te, non ce l'avrei mai fatta.
english: If it hadn't been for you, I would never have made it.
tip: Non fosse stato per te means 'had it not been for you'. Italian drops se and inverts the verb, just like formal English inverts 'had'.

target: Sia come sia, dobbiamo andare avanti.
english: Be that as it may, we must move forward.
tip: Sia come sia is a frozen phrase, literally 'be it as it be'. Both verbs are the subjunctive sia, matching English 'be that as it may'.

target: Ha assicurato che sarebbe arrivato puntuale alla cerimonia.
english: He assured us that he would arrive on time for the ceremony.
tip: In reported speech a future becomes the past conditional: arriverò turns into sarebbe arrivato, never arriverebbe.

target: A prescindere da ciò che abbiano deciso, noi proseguiremo.
english: Regardless of what they may have decided, we will continue.
tip: A prescindere da means 'regardless of'. The open-ended ciò che then pushes its verb into the subjunctive, hence abbiano deciso.

target: Avesse almeno avuto il coraggio di dirmelo in faccia.
english: If only he had had the courage to tell me to my face.
tip: With no se in front, Avesse almeno avuto means 'if only he had had'. A bare pluperfect subjunctive like this voices regret.

target: Pur essendo stanco, ha continuato.
english: Despite being tired, he continued.
tip: Pur essendo stanco means 'despite being tired'. Pur plus a gerund packs a whole 'although' clause into just two words.

target: Quale che sia la tua scelta, ti sosterrò.
english: Whatever your choice may be, I'll support you.
tip: Quale che sia: literary/formal 'whichever' with present subjunctive.
